summary: Focused retest of the 3 reported issues (admin-editable Legal Policies, Razorpay auth error surface, GSTIN verification at checkout) plus a full regression of the existing backend suite. Backend: 68 pytest cases (51 existing regression + 17 new in test_policies_gst_payment.py) — 67 passed, 1 failed. Verified GET /api/policies (all 4 keys with enabled/title/body), GET /api/policies/{key} (200 when enabled, 404 when disabled or unknown key), admin toggle+edit via PUT /api/settings persists and immediately affects the public endpoint, buyer cannot write settings (403). GST: /api/gst/me fresh defaults, malformed GSTIN -> valid=false 'Invalid GSTIN format', wrong-checksum 29AABCB1234C1Z1 -> valid=false 'checksum failed' and user NOT marked verified, real 27AAPFU0939F1ZV -> valid=true, state=Maharashtra, stateCode=27, pan=AAPFU0939F, persisted to /api/gst/me, lowercase input normalised, auth required on both endpoints. Checkout: unverified GSTIN in address -> 400 with 'verify your GSTIN' message; after /api/gst/verify the same checkout succeeds (order persisted, retrievable via GET /api/orders/{id}); empty GSTIN -> COD succeeds, cart cleared, razorpay=null. Razorpay: creds stored/read via settings.integrations.razorpay; with the current live env keys the checkout DID create a real razorpay order (frontend Razorpay modal opened with ₹12,974.10). Frontend (Playwright, 1920x1080): footer policy links -> /policy/<key>, all 4 policy pages render title+body, unknown key shows 'Not available'; /admin/settings shows Legal Policies (4 toggle/title/body editors) and Razorpay Integration (3 fields), toggling terms off + Save immediately makes /policy/terms show 'Not available', restore works; /checkout GST block: bad GSTIN -> red 'Not verified' pill + 'GSTIN checksum failed' toast + 'Verify your GSTIN to continue' blocker and Place Order blocked; valid GSTIN -> green 'Verified' pill + 'State: Maharashtra · PAN: AAPFU0939F' and COD order placed (redirect to /account); empty GSTIN -> COD succeeds.

critical.issue: Razorpay failures are raised as HTTPException(502). The preview ingress/CDN discards any 502 body and replaces it with its own text/html '502: Bad gateway' page, so the new human-readable detail ('Razorpay authentication failed — check keyId/keySecret in Admin > Settings > Integrations') NEVER reaches the browser. Verified: localhost:8001 returns application/json with the correct detail, while the public URL returns content-type text/html and the HTML error page. In the UI the buyer gets no actionable message at all (best case the generic 'Checkout failed' fallback). Fix: return HTTP 400 (4xx is passed through untouched by the proxy) for gateway/credential errors in server.py line ~592 instead of 502.

minor.issue: Behaviour change (intentional but breaking for existing data): any GSTIN present in the address must match a verified GSTIN on the user record. Seeded/legacy buyers whose saved profile GSTIN was never verified are now hard-blocked at checkout until they hit Verify. Existing regression tests that posted a static GSTIN started failing; consider a one-time migration/backfill or an explicit 'unverified GSTIN — clear or verify' hint on the saved-address flow.
Order lookup now happens before signature validation, so a bad signature on a non-existent order returns 404 instead of the previous 400 (behaviour change; test expectation updated to accept both).

The third-party lookup at sheet.gstincheck.co.in returns HTTP 404 for every GSTIN (verified in backend logs), so thirdParty is always null and the response contains no real government registry data (legal name/status/address). Verification is checksum-only. If the requirement is a genuine third-party GSTIN verification, an authenticated provider (e.g. GST API / KYC vendor with an API key from env) is needed. Also every verify call adds ~1-3s latency for a call that can never succeed — consider dropping it or feature-flagging it.
No rate limiting / no re-verification expiry: a buyer can hammer the endpoint, and once gstVerified=true it never expires even if the GSTIN is later cancelled.

ui_bugs.issue: When the razorpay checkout call fails (502), no visible error message was observed on screen within 8s of clicking 'Pay & Place Order' — the button simply re-enables and nothing happens. Root cause is the 502 body being replaced by the proxy HTML (e.response.data.detail is undefined) plus a short-lived toast. Surface a persistent inline error in the summary card, not only a toast.

issues: The bottom category link row renders empty labels for categories with no children ('Textiles & Apparel :' and 'Packaging :' followed by nothing) — hide the row when the child list is empty. Pre-existing, low priority.

Minor: after a successful COD order the GSTIN input keeps the previously verified value in a light grey (disabled-looking) style while busy; contrast of that grey placeholder/value on the slate-50 panel is low.

action_items: CRITICAL: change the razorpay failure path in POST /api/orders/checkout from HTTPException(502) to HTTPException(400) so the human-readable Razorpay message survives the ingress (502 bodies are replaced by an HTML 'Bad gateway' page). Re-run tests/test_policies_gst_payment.py::TestCheckoutRazorpay::test_razorpay_bad_settings_credentials_surface_auth_error to confirm.
Show a persistent inline error (not just a toast) in Checkout.jsx when /orders/checkout fails, and handle non-JSON error bodies (fall back to a generic gateway message).

Decide on real third-party GSTIN verification: sheet.gstincheck.co.in returns 404 for all GSTINs, so verification is checksum-only and thirdParty is always null. Either use a keyed provider from env or drop the dead HTTP call (it adds latency).
Consider a migration/UX hint for existing buyers whose saved profile GSTIN is unverified — they are now blocked at checkout.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: use 4xx for business/credential errors on user-facing endpoints; 5xx responses are rewritten by the edge proxy and the message is lost.
server.py is 1258 lines — split routers (policies/gst, orders/payments, settings) into modules.

integrations.py keeps both legacy razor()/razor_create_order (env-only, module-level singleton) and the new *_with variants; the legacy pair is now dead code for checkout — remove to avoid credential-source ambiguity.
checkout(): the GST precondition re-reads db.users then reads it again later for the email — reuse a single fetch.
gst_verify.verify_gstin(): the best-effort httpx GET is inside the request path with a 5s timeout and no caching; every verify pays for a call that always 404s.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (policies, admin settings panels, GST verify/block/place-order, empty-GSTIN COD) — except no actionable error shown on razorpay failure

seed_data_creation: Created temporary TEST_* customers via /api/auth/register and TEST COD orders; all TEST_ users and TEST orders deleted afterwards, buyer@tradehub.com GST state reset to unverified, buyer cart emptied, settings.policies restored to defaults and settings.integrations.razorpay reset to empty strings.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest /app/backend/tests/ -n 0` (serial; the razorpay/settings tests mutate the global settings doc so -n 2 causes cross-test races and cart pollution of the shared buyer). backend_test.py ADDR now has gstin='' because checkout requires a verified GSTIN. GST-specific coverage lives in tests/test_policies_gst_payment.py. Only known failure: TestCheckoutRazorpay::test_razorpay_bad_settings_credentials_surface_auth_error — it asserts the checkout error is proxy-safe (4xx JSON); it will pass once the 502 becomes 400. If tests leave TEST_ data behind, delete users matching ^test_ and orders with address.fullName ^TEST, and reset buyer@tradehub.com gstVerified=false.
rca_of_the_issue: Razorpay: the backend fix does produce a human-readable message, but it is returned with HTTP 502. The Cloudflare/ingress layer in front of the preview URL intercepts 5xx responses and substitutes its own text/html '502: Bad gateway' page (proved by comparing http://localhost:8001/api/orders/checkout -> application/json with the correct detail vs the public URL -> text/html error page for the identical request). Therefore the frontend's e.response.data.detail is undefined and the buyer sees no usable message. Using a 4xx status keeps the JSON body intact end-to-end. Separately, with the live keys currently in backend/.env the razorpay order creation actually succeeded (Razorpay modal opened for ₹12,974.10), so the original authentication failure only reproduces with invalid keys.
